clue.text: Maybe Leo and Zoe's faith in God somehow constant?

indicators.note: somehow says these words reach the answer in some other order, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A query whether a man and a woman's religious faith might be unwavering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo' looks like a man's name partnering Zoe, but it is the lion of the zodiac; 'Maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve astrological star signs, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Studio may notice struggling TV show

indicators.note: struggling suggests things going badly and in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A studio might observe that a television programme is doing badly in the ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a genre of television series built around recurring characters in comic situations.

clue.text: Spurs game held up by commercials

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, supported from below

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
ads are television or radio commercials

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur's match being delayed by advertising breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurs' reads as the football club, but it is a verb: urges on.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone and to goad them both mean to prod or urge them into action.

clue.text: Odd person bored by Edrich at first, and batsmen like Boycott?

indicators.note: bored by means drilled into, so the next piece goes inside the jumbled letters
odd here means strange or out of place, signalling that the letters of the next word are rearranged
at first takes only the opening letter of Edrich

explanation.surface: A strange individual drilled by the England cricketer Edrich, and other batsmen like Geoffrey Boycott.
explanation.walkthrough: John Edrich and Geoffrey Boycott were both England opening batsmen, so the surface stays in the cricket scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England opening batsman, one who starts the innings, so batsmen like him fit.

clue.text: Belts and backpacks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belts means moves very fast
second meaning: backpacks as a verb means tours on a budget carrying a rucksack

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns for things you carry or wear; read as verbs, each is a way of going somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeding along and touring with a rucksack are both kinds of journeying from place to place.

clue.text: Mournful English member going over first clue?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above the next one, going over it

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the first clue in this puzzle is 1 across, written 1ac with the 1 as Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sad Englishman's limb passing over the opening clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword clue references are shortened to number plus 'ac' or 'dn', so 1 across becomes I AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead, so it means sorrowful.

clue.text: Remarkable person tackling intrusive photographer in writing

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the photographer is gripped inside

parts.note: a oner is British slang for a remarkable or unique person
a pap is short for paparazzo, a press photographer who intrudes on celebrities

explanation.surface: An extraordinary celebrity rugby-tackling a pushy press photographer, written up for the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set down on paper is recorded in written form rather than spoken.

clue.text: Sand in water is so unlike this clue!

definitions.text: Sand in water is so unlike this clue!

parts.words: Sand in water is so unlike this clue
parts.note: sand will not dissolve in water, whereas a clue can be solved, so the word fits sand but not the clue

explanation.walkthrough: The word has two senses: unable to dissolve and unable to be solved. Sand has the first, while this clue, being solvable, lacks the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand does not dissolve in water, and a puzzle without a solution is equally described by this adjective.

clue.text: Unwanted visitor to arrive after Mass in state of daft optimism

indicators.note: after puts the visitor and arrival behind the mass

parts.note: a cloud is a mass, as in a cloud of smoke
the cuckoo lays its eggs in other birds' nests, an unwelcome guest
to land is to arrive at a destination

explanation.surface: An unwelcome guest turning up after church, in a mood of foolish hopefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as the church service but gives a mass of vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Aristophanes' The Birds, describes a fanciful realm of unrealistic hopes and dreams.

clue.text: Firm handle

parts.note: a firm is a business and a handle is slang for a name, so a business's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm handle' suggests a strong grip on a door, but it means the name a company trades under.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the brand or business name under which a company sells its products.

clue.text: Trouble over sauce

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, something that causes trouble
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Difficulty about a sauce at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, parmesan and olive oil.

clue.text: Matthau stereotyped, somewhat unsmiling

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The actor Walter Matthau being typecast as rather grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and stern in manner, without warmth or humour.

clue.text: Run through both sides of item with China news chief

indicators.note: both sides of keeps the first and last letters of item

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and a mate is a pal
ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Running through the edges of a story with a Chinese news boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in rhyming slang china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce through with a sharp point, as a sword runs someone through.

clue.text: No end of sheep in spring meadow

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to leap is to spring, as a lamb does

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of sheep

explanation.surface: No lamb bounding in spring meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for a grassy field or pasture.

clue.text: Engineer iciness cuts into

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An engineer's frostiness cuts deep.
explanation.definitionFit: To incise is to make a cut with a sharp tool, as an engraver or surgeon does.

clue.text: Pleasant canoeing around lake

indicators.note: around means turned about and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Paddling a canoe around a lake makes for an agreeable time.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial means agreeable and suited to one's taste, like friendly company.

clue.text: I for one must sit on top of omnibus

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of omnibus

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they personally must ride on the top deck of a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I for one' reads as a phrase, but 'I' alone is the definition and 'for one' gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the sense of oneself that says I.

clue.text: California kid joins you, heading off for deer

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
to kid and to rib both mean to tease

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of you

explanation.surface: A Californian youngster teams up with you before setting off after deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child, but it is a verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large migratory member of the deer family.

clue.text: Brilliant diamond?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a playing card of the diamond suit, its top card, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: A brilliant is also a cut of diamond, so the clue looks like one description of a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word praises something superb and also names the single-pip card in each suit, including diamonds.

clue.text: Partners wearing nothing from the waist up all the time?

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece goes about the other

parts.note: wearing no top means being bare above the waist
North and South are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: A couple going topless constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S, North and South, partner each other at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means without pause or interruption, continuing throughout.

clue.text: Incorrectly, three and two wife omitted in addition

indicators.note: incorrectly means not in the right order, so the letters are rearranged
omitted means left out, so a letter goes

explanation.surface: A sum done wrongly, three and two, with a married woman left out of the reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W out of TWO to leave TO, then rearrange THREE plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal word meaning besides that, or to that thing, adding on.

clue.text: Fuss with black mint, perhaps

parts.note: a pother is a commotion or fuss
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Making a fuss about a dark mint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is any herb grown for the kitchen pot, and mint is one example.

clue.text: Last third of September initially sent Queen and King crazy

parts.note: September has nine letters, and its final three are BER

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of sent

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Late September news drove the royal couple mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Berserk means wildly out of control, from the frenzied Norse warriors called berserkers.

clue.text: Working with Greek character to support British Airways

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below the first

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Working alongside a Greek figure to prop up the national airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Airways' reads as the airline; split it, and 'Airways' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the two main air passages branching from the windpipe into the lungs.

clue.text: Ponder again on lean rump of pork

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
lean and thin both mean without fat

indicators.note: rump of means the tail end, the last letter of pork

explanation.surface: Reconsidering a meal of lean pork rump.
explanation.definitionFit: To rethink is to consider something afresh and perhaps change one's mind.

clue.text: Paddle boat edging away, meeting little resistance

indicators.note: edging away removes the outer letters of boat

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance, a little abbreviation

explanation.surface: A boat drifting off but meeting only slight opposition from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a long pole with a blade used to row or propel a boat.

clue.text: Essentially fear getting trapped in open gorge

indicators.note: getting trapped in puts the middle letters inside the other word

parts.note: overt means done openly, not hidden

indicators.note: essentially takes the core of fear, its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Basically, fear of being caught in an exposed ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' reads as a ravine, but it is a verb: to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge oneself is to stuff oneself with food, eating far too much.

clue.text: Busy one taking time with husband ahead of leave

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the time and husband go inside

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A hectic person fitting in time with her husband before departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is constantly active and occupied, never resting.

clue.text: She inspires scoundrel hiding in central León?

indicators.note: hiding in puts the scoundrel inside the central letters
central takes the middle two letters of León

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain lurking in the middle of the Spanish city of León.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek muse of lyric and love poetry, a source of inspiration for poets.

clue.text: Now and then, jelly is the best

indicators.note: now and then means occasionally, so only every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Jelly, eaten occasionally, is the finest dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top group, the finest people in a society.

clue.text: Coming back, spots entertaining artist with hot food

indicators.note: coming back means returning, so the whole is read in reverse
entertaining means hosting, so the spots hold the next pieces

parts.note: acne is an outbreak of spots
Salvador Dali was the surrealist artist
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: On return, a spotty person hosts a painter and some spicy food.
explanation.walkthrough: Put DALI and H inside ACNE to make ADALIHCNE, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla filled and covered with chilli sauce.

clue.text: Next to Wimpy Bar, reportedly cycled in Dorothy's way

indicators.note: next to places the cowardly word beside the following pieces

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, wimpy
a brick is a bar-shaped block, as in a gold brick

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: cycled means rode a bike

explanation.surface: Someone rode a bicycle past a Wimpy fast-food bar, as it is told.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimpy is a British hamburger chain, so 'Wimpy Bar' looks like one place.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Wizard of Oz, Dorothy follows a golden-paved path to the Emerald City.
